1. 사울이 죽은 후 다윗의 행보\n - 사무엘하서는 1장부터 24장까지:
1. David's course after Saul's death
 - 2 Samuel, from chapter 1 all the way to 24, is entirely David's story.
<삼하1:1~10> 사울의 죽은 후라 다윗이 아말렉 사람을 도륙하고 돌아: <2 Sam 1:1~10> Now it came to pass after the death of Saul, when David was returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had abode two days in Ziklag; it came even to pass on the third day, that, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul with his clothes rent, and earth upon his head: and so it was, when he came to David, that he fell to the earth, and did obeisance. And David said unto him,
대답하되 이스라엘 진에서 도망하여 왔나이다: And he said unto him, Out of the camp of Israel am I escaped.
다윗이 가로되 일이 어떻게 되었느뇨 너는 내게 고하라: And David said unto him, How went the matter? I pray thee, tell me.
저가 대답하되 군사가 전쟁 중에서 도망하기도 하였고 무리 중에 엎드러져: And he answered, That the people are fled from the battle, and many of the people also are fallen and dead; and Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.
다윗이 자기에게 고하는 소년에게 묻되 사울과 그 아들 요나단의 죽은 줄을: And David said unto the young man that told him, How knowest thou that Saul and Jonathan his son be dead?
그에게 고하는 소년이 가로되 내가 우연히 길보아 산에 올라보니 사울이 자: And the young man that told him said, As I happened by chance upon mount Gilboa, behold, Saul leaned upon his spear; and, lo, the chariots and horsemen followed hard after him. And when he looked behind him, he saw me, and called unto me. And I answered, Here am I. And he said unto me, Who art thou? And I answered him, I am an Amalekite. He said unto me again, Stand, I pray thee, upon me, and slay me: for anguish is come upon me, because my life is yet whole in me. So I stood upon him, and slew him, because I was sure that he could not live after that he was fallen: and I took the crown that was upon his head, and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them hither unto my lord.
얘가 지금 거짓말 하고 있죠? 사무엘상서 끝을 읽어 봤기 때문에 이 아이: This guy is lying right now, isn't he? Since we've read the end of 1 Samuel, we can tell right away that this young man is lying.
‘니가 지금 하나님의 기름 부으신 사울을 죽였다는거냐? 밖에 아무도 없느: ‘You're telling me you killed Saul, God's anointed? Is anybody out there?’
바로 데려가 목을 쳐 버립니다. 이런 놈은 여차하면 다윗의 목을 잘라서: He has him taken away and beheaded on the spot. A guy like this would cut off David's head too the moment it suited him and go offer it to someone else. Saul and David were political rivals, so he thought he'd get a reward for bringing Saul's head, but that's only because he didn't know David.
<삼하1:17~18> 다윗이 이 슬픈 노래로 사울과 그 아들 요나단을 조: <2 Sam 1:17~18> And David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son, and he bade them teach it to the children of Judah, the song of the bow: behold, it is written in the book of Jasher.
자기를 죽이려고 했던 사울의 죽음을 슬퍼하는 노래를 지어서 유다 족속에게: He writes a song mourning the death of Saul, the man who tried to kill him, and tells the tribe of Judah to mourn together with him. A trick like that boy's doesn't work on a man like this. The book of Jasher comes up here, and a footnote says it's quoted from the book of Jasher, which was written before the books of Samuel.
<삼하2:1> 그 후에 다윗이 여호와께 물어 가로되 내가 유다 한 성으로: <2 Sam 2:1> And it came to pass after this, that David enquired of the LORD, saying, Shall I go up into any of the cities of Judah? And the LORD said unto him, Go up. And David said, Whither shall I go up? And he said, Unto Hebron.
David doesn't make rash political moves; he asks God about each thing, one by one.
4절 보시면 유다 지파 사람들이 다윗을 왕으로 세우고 나서는 일러 바칩니: Look at verse 4: after the men of the tribe of Judah make David king, they go and tell on someone. That the men of Jabesh-gilead buried Saul. Didn't these people hear about the Amalekite boy who lied and died....
다윗은 오히려 길르앗 야베스 사람들을 칭찬해요. 전에 길르앗 야베스 사람: David instead praises the men of Jabesh-gilead. You see, once before, when the men of Jabesh-gilead were nearly wiped out, Saul had rescued them.
사울이 죽고 요나단, 아비나답, 말기수아도 죽었으니 다윗이 치고 올라가: Saul is dead, and Jonathan, Abinadab and Malchishua are dead too, so people are quietly watching David's moves, thinking, won't David march up and become king? But David doesn't act rashly; in Hebron he became king over the tribe of Judah only.
<삼하2:8~9> 사울의 군장 넬의 아들 아브넬이 이미 사울의 아들 이스: <2 Sam 2:8~9> But Abner the son of Ner, captain of Saul's host, took Ish-bosheth the son of Saul, and brought him over to Mahanaim; and made him king over Gilead, and over the Ashurites, and over Jezreel, and over Ephraim, and over Benjamin, and over all Israel.
사울 왕가에 남아있던 왕자 이스보셋이라고 있는데 이 사람은 두 발을 못쓰:
There was a prince left in Saul's royal house called Ish-bosheth, and he was lame, unable to use both feet. So they put Ish-bosheth up front as a figurehead, and Abner holds the real power and faces off against David. At this time Israel goes through an unstable two-year period as a divided kingdom.
 - Verse 12. Before long the two sides go to battle at the pool of Gibeon. At first they agreed to settle it with 12 men each and end it there. But once they actually clashed, they thought, while we're winning, let's just wipe them out, and fought, and Ish-bosheth's army, 360 men, collapses in an instant. And looking at it, only 19 of David's army died.
그러니 백전노장 아브넬이 승산이 없다고 판단하고 후퇴함. 그런데 그 뒤를: So Abner, a seasoned veteran, judges that he can't win and retreats. But Joab's younger brother Asahel chases after him. The name Asahel is 'make + God', God's feet.
‘군복이나 하나 벗겨서 돌아가라’: ‘Just strip a soldier of his armor and go back.’
‘웃기시네. 영감쟁이 오늘 끝장을 보자’: ‘Yeah, right. Old man, let's finish this today.’
창을 옆구리 사이로 빼서 급브레이크. 아사헬 사망: He thrusts the spear backward past his side, slams on the brakes. Asahel dies.
그 소식을 듣고 요압이 쫓아 갔지만 정면 승부를 하자는 아브넬의 말에 기: Joab hears the news and chases after him, but when Abner proposes a head-on fight, he loses his nerve and turns back. With his heart full of a grudge... his brother is dead, his pride is crushed...
<삼하3:6> 사울의 집과 다윗의 집 사이에 전쟁이 있는 동안에 아브넬이:
<2 Sam 3:6> And it came to pass, while there was war between the house of Saul and the house of David, that Abner made himself strong for the house of Saul.
 - Abner held the real power, and he went after Saul's concubine Rizpah. And Ish-bosheth, being "king" and all, said a word to Abner, huh?
그러니까 아브넬이 ‘내가 유다의 개 대가리인 줄 알아? 내가 오늘 너를: So Abner says, ‘Do you think I'm a dog's head for Judah? I haven't handed you over to David to this day, and you get angry at me over one woman?’ and threatens to hand the whole kingdom over to David.
He sends men to David: I'll hand it all over to you.  But in return, no political revenge.
<삼하3:13> 다윗이 가로되 좋다 내가 너와 언약하려니와 내가 네게 한:
<2 Sam 3:13> And he said, Well; I will make a league with thee: but one thing I require of thee, that is, Thou shalt not see my face, except thou first bring Michal Saul's daughter, when thou comest to see my face.
 - Michal had been married to another man for over 10 years, and he brings her back again. And then Abner goes to David with only 20 attendants. David, too, receives Abner courteously.
 - But the problem is Joab. Hearing that Abner is going back, he sends someone: ‘Tell him I'd like a word with him.’ From Abner's side too, Joab was a mountain he had to get over, so he goes to meet Joab without suspicion. David didn't know.
요압 이 나쁜 놈이 아브넬과 귓속말을 하려는 척~ 하면서 칼로 푹 찔러: This rotten Joab pretends~ to whisper in Abner's ear and stabs him to death with a sword. Because Abner killed his brother, he takes personal revenge. Just at the moment when north and south were about to become one in peace, Joab goes and does this.
다음 날 신문 1면에 대문짝만하게 나면서 여론이 막 죽 끓듯 해요. 그런:
The next day it's splashed across the front page, and public opinion boils over. But David shows up at the funeral, wails loudly, and truly grieves Abner's death. People go, "Turns out it wasn't David, it was Joab taking personal revenge," and the people's hearts surge back to David like a wave.
 - Chapter 4 tells of Ish-bosheth's assassination: Rechab and Baanah killed him, cut off Ish-bosheth's head and brought it to David, and he said, "I even killed the guy who lied about killing Saul, and you, who really killed him, expect to live? Is anybody out there?" and dealt with them on the spot.
 - Even after bringing Michal back, David still had many important national matters. He attacked Jerusalem, which the Jebusites held (chapter 5), and he also brings up the ark (chapter 6) that was at Kiriath-jearim. But in bringing up the ark, David makes a mistake.
 - The ark is supposed to be carried on the shoulders of the priests, but David didn't know that and tried to bring it on a cart, and Uzzah dies. So, afraid, he leaves it at the house of Obed-edom. Hey, what's Obed-edom supposed to do? God blessed him. So he goes to bring it again, and this time he'd done his homework and had the priests carry it.
너무 신이 나서 다윗이 옷이 벗겨지는 줄도 모르고 춤을 춰요. 그걸 보고:
David is so overjoyed he dances without even realizing his clothes are coming off. Seeing that, Michal mocks him. From then on David doesn't see Michal. It's recorded, you know, 'she had no child unto the day of her death.'  From Michal's side too, she'd been living happily with another man, was torn away and brought back, and David doesn't even come to see her once, so she must have been sulking.
 - The incident that broke out after this one with Michal is the Bathsheba incident. Of course David was wrong a hundred times, a thousand times over, but when you trace cause and effect, you can't say Michal had no share in it. What's amazing is that even seeing such an ugly crime, the loyal people around him, like Nathan, Benaiah and Zadok, serve David just the same as before. And the most loyal man of all was Uriah the Hittite.
- In chapter 7, David wants to build the temple, and when he tells Nathan he wants to build it, Nathan says, ‘You're the king, do as you please,’ but God stops him. He has too much blood on his hands. If a man who ruled by force says, I'm going to build a temple, so give some donations, what would come in isn't donations but flattery money, right?
 - Instead, God promises, ‘You want to build Me a house? I will build you a house.’
In chapters 8, 9 and 10 he keeps winning battle after battle. Wherever he went, he won.
 - Chapter 9 is the story of David taking care of Saul's family. David doesn't forget Jonathan's kindness -> he takes care of Mephibosheth. "That thou shouldest look upon such a dead dog as I am!!" He's deeply moved. A man lame in both feet.
 - Chapter 11 is that famous Bathsheba incident
다윗의 죄악 - 밧세바를 보고 음욕을 품은 것, 그것을 실행에 옮긴 것,:
David's sins: he looked at Bathsheba and lusted, he acted on it, in the process he killed his most loyal servant, and in the end he just took her.  The Ten Commandments said, do not covet your neighbor's wife..
 - Chapter 12. After that crime, Nathan comes and points out his sin, and David falls on his face right away.
<삼하12:14> 이 일로 인하여 여호와의 원수로 크게 훼방할 거리를 얻:
<2 Sam 12:14> Howbeit, because by this deed thou hast given great occasion to the enemies of the LORD to blaspheme, the child also that is born unto thee shall surely die.
 - Sin gives Satan something to blaspheme with.
 - Meanwhile, the child Bathsheba bore falls ill and dies, and after that they have another child and call him Solomon, which comes from shalom. David, who fought so many wars, longed for peace... Solomon's other name is Jedidiah. Because they were worried he'd die too, God gave the child the name Jedidiah, meaning "I love him." This will be on the test.
<13:1a> 그 후에 이 일이 있으니라\n - 밑줄 쫙~ 이것이 바로:
<13:1a> And it came to pass after this,
 - Underline that~ This is exactly the historian's eye. After David's terrible crime, ominous things start happening in David's house.
 - Amnon falls for Absalom's sister Tamar, rapes her and throws her out; Absalom, enraged, kills Amnon; Absalom runs away, comes back, and starts a rebellion, and David goes through absolute hell. In the end Absalom dies too. This time again that rascal Joab didn't listen and killed him, right?
이런 일들이 전부 어디에 걸려있다? 그 후에 이 일이 있으니라. 이 한:
What do all these things hang on? "And it came to pass after this." They all hang on this one phrase.
 - So David puts down Absalom's rebellion and returns to Jerusalem, and at that point who's in the most awkward spot? When David was fleeing, Shimei, thinking David was finished, poured curses on him and taunted him, right? David forgives him too. That makes the top headline on the front page of the Kookmin Ilbo.
다윗이 이런거 보면 정치 9단이야. 다윗이 얼마나 어진 임금인지, 시므이: When you see things like this, David was a political grandmaster. Shimei becomes a walking billboard for how kind a king David is. But later, David hands Solomon a hit list, and Shimei's name is on it. I kept him alive because I needed him, but you don't need him, you get it?
그리고 뒤늦게 다윗이 살뜰하게 챙겼던 므비보셋이 다윗을 맞으러 나왔는데: And then, late, Mephibosheth, whom David had so carefully looked after, comes out to meet David
‘ 므비보셋이여 네가 어찌하여 나와 함께 가지 아니하였는뇨?’: ‘ Mephibosheth, why didn't you go with me?’
‘왕이여 나는 절름발이라 빨리 갈 수가 없는데 내 종이 나를 속이고 먼저: ‘O king, I am lame and couldn't go fast, and my servant deceived me, went ahead, and slandered me.’
그 전에 종이 먼저 다윗을 맞이해서 다윗이 그 종에게 므비보셋의 밭을 다: Before that, the servant had met David first, and David had told that servant to take all of Mephibosheth's fields, right? This guy's name is Ziba, and when David tells him to divide the fields again with that son of a Ziba, Mephibosheth says, ‘It's enough for me that the king has come back alive. Tell that son of a Ziba to keep the property all to himself.’
그리고 다윗이 도망 갈 때 도움을 줬던 바르실래를 만나서 ‘나와 함께 예: And he meets Barzillai, who had helped him when he was fleeing: ‘Come with me to Jerusalem. I'll give you a position.’ ‘I'm old, and I can't even taste my food. Here is my son Chimham; if he's useful to you, take him and use him,’ he says, so David takes Chimham back with him.
상과 벌을 확실하게 하죠?\n - 21장에는:
He's clear about rewards and punishments, right?
 - In chapter 21
3년간 기근이 있었다는 얘기가 나옵니다. 사울 왕이 기브온 족속을 인종:
there's a story of a famine for 3 years. King Saul had once tried to ethnically cleanse the Gibeonites, and that grievance ran so deep that it wouldn't rain. So to settle the Gibeonites' grievance, Saul's descendants had to be handed over, and even then David is very careful, worried it might look like political revenge. So he spares Mephibosheth and hands over others. And after that, it rained again.
 - Chapter 22 and the beginning of chapter 23 have songs of praise.  Similar content to Psalm 18.
<삼하22:5~6> 사망의 물결이 나를 에우고 불의의 창수가 나를 두렵게:
<2 Sam 22:5~6> When the waves of death compassed me, the floods of ungodly men made me afraid; the sorrows of hell compassed me about; the snares of death prevented me;
 - Death was always brushing past David's neck, and at night he'd be pinned down by nightmares of death; even going through such hard days, he was a man who never bent his integrity and uprightness, his convictions and his principles.
우리가 정직하고 순전하게 살기 위해서는 손해보는 연습부터 해야 한다. 룻:
For us to live honestly and with integrity, we first have to practice taking a loss. In Ruth, too, there was a man who refused to raise up his brother's inheritance because he was afraid he'd lose out, right? If you're set on never taking a loss, you end up doing things you shouldn't do.
 - Apart from the incident with Bathsheba, Uriah's wife, David made almost no mistakes, and even in that incident he took his discipline meekly and showed humility
<삼하23:3~4> 이스라엘의 하나님이 말씀하시며 이스라엘의 바위가 내게:
<2 Sam 23:3~4> The God of Israel said, the Rock of Israel spake to me, He that ruleth over men must be just, ruling in the fear of God. And he shall be as the light of the morning, when the sun riseth, even a morning without clouds; as the tender grass springing out of the earth by clear shining after rain.
 - Ruling people with justice and ruling in the fear of God. That's exactly what politics is. Korea's politicians really ought to learn a thing or two from David
 -  Chapter 23 talks about David's men and their exploits, and they're amazing people.
 - David's three mighty men: Josheb-basshebeth, Eleazar, Shammah
 - Chapter 24 has the scene where, after all the troubles have passed, David gets puffed up, takes a census, and gets into serious trouble.
- Verse 1: ‘The LORD stirred David up in order to strike Israel.’
대상 21:1에는 같은 사건을 두고 ‘사탄이 이스라엘을 대적하고 다윗을: 1 Chr 21:1, about the same event, says ‘Satan stood up against Israel and provoked David.’
같은 사건을 두고 양편이 다른 시각으로 바라봄. 거시적인 안목에서 보면: The two sides look at the same event from different angles. Seen from the big picture, Satan stirred him up with God's permission. Or you could say God simply didn't stop Satan from stirring him up.
선지자 갓이 임하여 세 가지 중 하나를 고르게 함: The prophet Gad comes and makes him choose one of three things
3번을 선택함. 핑계 - 사람은 무섭다. 하나님은 긍휼이 있으시니까 하나:
He chooses number 3. His excuse: people are frightening. God is merciful, so I'll take it from God. So he's disciplined, and he offers a sacrifice; he buys the threshing floor of Araunah and sacrifices to God there, and the pestilence stops. The temple was built on that spot.
 - The reason I talked about Abraham and David at such length is that God introduces Jesus as the son of Abraham and the son of David. We'll now be looking at the books of Kings, the stories of the kings, and they're evaluated simply. For the northern kingdom of Israel: they followed the sin of Jeroboam. For the southern kingdom of Judah: they did as David did. Or didn't.
